def prepare_data_loader(
    dataloader: DataLoader,
    device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
    num_processes: Optional[int] = None,
    process_index: Optional[int] = None,
    split_batches: bool = False,
    put_on_device: bool = False,
    rng_types: Optional[list[Union[str, RNGType]]] = None,
    dispatch_batches: Optional[bool] = None,
    even_batches: bool = True,
    slice_fn_for_dispatch: Optional[Callable] = None,
    use_seedable_sampler: bool = False,
    data_seed: Optional[int] = None,
    non_blocking: bool = False,
    use_stateful_dataloader: bool = False,
    torch_device_mesh=None,
) -> DataLoader:
    """
    Wraps a PyTorch `DataLoader` to generate batches for one of the processes only.

    Depending on the value of the `drop_last` attribute of the `dataloader` passed, it will either stop the iteration
    at the first batch that would be too small / not present on all processes or loop with indices from the beginning.

    Args:
        dataloader (`torch.utils.data.dataloader.DataLoader`):
            The data loader to split across several devices.
        device (`torch.device`):
            The target device for the returned `DataLoader`.
        num_processes (`int`, *optional*):
            The number of processes running concurrently. Will default to the value given by [`~state.PartialState`].
        process_index (`int`, *optional*):
            The index of the current process. Will default to the value given by [`~state.PartialState`].
        split_batches (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
            Whether the resulting `DataLoader` should split the batches of the original data loader across devices or
            yield full batches (in which case it will yield batches starting at the `process_index`-th and advancing of
            `num_processes` batches at each iteration).

            Another way to see this is that the observed batch size will be the same as the initial `dataloader` if
            this option is set to `True`, the batch size of the initial `dataloader` multiplied by `num_processes`
            otherwise.

            Setting this option to `True` requires that the batch size of the `dataloader` is a round multiple of
            `batch_size`.
        put_on_device (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
            Whether or not to put the batches on `device` (only works if the batches are nested list, tuples or
            dictionaries of tensors).
        rng_types (list of `str` or [`~utils.RNGType`]):
            The list of random number generators to synchronize at the beginning of each iteration. Should be one or
            several of:

            - `"torch"`: the base torch random number generator
            - `"cuda"`: the CUDA random number generator (GPU only)
            - `"xla"`: the XLA random number generator (TPU only)
            - `"generator"`: the `torch.Generator` of the sampler (or batch sampler if there is no sampler in your
              dataloader) or of the iterable dataset (if it exists) if the underlying dataset is of that type.

        dispatch_batches (`bool`, *optional*):
            If set to `True`, the dataloader prepared is only iterated through on the main process and then the batches
            are split and broadcast to each process. Will default to `True` when the underlying dataset is an
            `IterableDataset`, `False` otherwise.
        even_batches (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
            If set to `True`, in cases where the total batch size across all processes does not exactly divide the
            dataset, samples at the start of the dataset will be duplicated so the batch can be divided equally among
            all workers.
        slice_fn_for_dispatch (`Callable`, *optional*`):
            If passed, this function will be used to slice tensors across `num_processes`. Will default to
            [`~utils.slice_tensors`]. This argument is used only when `dispatch_batches` is set to `True` and will be
            ignored otherwise.
        use_seedable_sampler (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
            Whether to use the [`~data_loader.SeedableRandomSampler`] instead of a `RandomSampler` for better
            reproducibility. Comes at a cost of potentially different performances due to different shuffling
            algorithms but ensures results will be the *exact* same. Should be paired with `set_seed()` at every
            `self.set_epoch`
        data_seed (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `None`):
            The seed to use for the underlying generator when using `use_seedable_sampler`. If `None`, the generator
            will use the current default seed from torch.
        non_blocking (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
            If set to `True`, dataloader will utilize non-blocking host-to-device transfers. If the dataloader has
            `pin_memory` set to `True`, this will help to increase overlap between data transfer and computations.
        use_stateful_dataloader (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
            "If set to true, the dataloader prepared by the Accelerator will be backed by "
            "[torchdata.StatefulDataLoader](https://github.com/pytorch/data/tree/main/torchdata/stateful_dataloader).
            This requires `torchdata` version 0.8.0 or higher that supports StatefulDataLoader to be installed."
        torch_device_mesh (`torch.distributed.DeviceMesh`, *optional*, defaults to `None`):
            PyTorch device mesh.


    Returns:
        `torch.utils.data.dataloader.DataLoader`: A new data loader that will yield the portion of the batches

    <Tip warning={true}>

    `BatchSampler`s with varying batch sizes are not enabled by default. To enable this behaviour, set `even_batches`
    equal to `False`

    </Tip>
    """
    if dispatch_batches is None:
        if not put_on_device:
            dispatch_batches = False
        else:
            dispatch_batches = isinstance(dataloader.dataset, IterableDataset)

    if dispatch_batches and not put_on_device:
        raise ValueError("Using `dispatch_batches=True` requires `put_on_device=True`.")
    # Grab defaults from PartialState
    state = PartialState()
    if num_processes is None:
        num_processes = state.num_processes

    if process_index is None:
        process_index = state.process_index

    if torch_device_mesh:
        if state.distributed_type == DistributedType.DEEPSPEED:
            # In DeepSpeed, the optimizer sharing level in DP is determined by the config file.
            # Only considers "dp" and "tp".
            # Given a device mesh (dp, tp) = (2, 3):
            # - From the data parallel perspective, ranks should be structured as: 0 0 0 1 1 1
            # - Processes with the same DP rank will receive the same batch.
            submesh_tp_size = 1
            if "tp" in torch_device_mesh.mesh_dim_names:
                submesh_tp_size = torch_device_mesh["tp"].size()
            process_index = process_index // submesh_tp_size
            num_processes = num_processes // submesh_tp_size
        else:
            # when device mesh is used, specifically with TP
            # then there is need to update process_index and num_processes
            # to bring in the effect of generating same batch across TP ranks
            # and different batch across FSDP and DP ranks.
            # Example:
            # if device mesh is (dp,fsdp,tp) = (2, 2, 3)
            # ranks would range from 0...11
            # from data angle ranks should look like 0 0 0 1 1 1 2 2 2 3 3 3
            # processes with same ranks/ids would receive the same batch
            # for CP the same as TP applies
            submesh_fsdp_size = 1
            submesh_dp_size = 1

            batch_size=dataloader.batch_size,
            rng_types=rng_types,
            _drop_last=dataloader.drop_last,
            _non_blocking=non_blocking,
            synchronized_generator=synchronized_generator,

```python
# Flush user-logged metrics (from log_metric). A metric may be logged on some ranks only (e.g. a reward
        # function guarded by a rank check), so the pending key sets can differ per rank. Iterating the local dict
```
        # alone would make some ranks enter `accelerator.gather` while others skip it, desynchronizing the
        # collective backend at the first generation batch. Instead, gather the union of names — a collective every
        # rank joins identically — then issue one gather per unioned name on every rank. Ranks that logged nothing
        # for a name contribute NaN and the mean is NaN-aware, so an absent rank neither breaks the collectives nor
        # dilutes the logged value with a zero.
        names_per_rank = gather_object(sorted(self._pending_metrics))
        for name in sorted(set().union(*map(set, names_per_rank))):
            values = self._pending_metrics.get(name, [])
            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values) if values else float("nan")
            local_tensor = torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(local_tensor).nanmean().item()
            self._metrics[mode][name].append(global_mean)
        self._pending_metrics.clear()

    def log(self, logs: dict[str, float], start_time: float | None = None) -> None:
        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
        # Average the metrics
        metrics = {}
        for key, val in self._metrics[mode].items():
            # Filter out NaN values before averaging. A reward function that returns None for all samples
            # in a batch produces NaN for that batch's metric. With logging_steps > 1, a naive sum()/len()
            # would let a single NaN contaminate valid data from other batches. Only return None when no
            # valid values remain (e.g. JSON loggers crash on float NaN).
            valid = [v for v in val if not math.isnan(v)]
            metrics[key] = sum(valid) / len(valid) if valid else None

        # This method can be called both in training and evaluation. When called in evaluation, the keys in `logs`
        # start with "eval_". We need to add the prefix "eval_" to the keys in `metrics` to match the format.
        if mode == "eval":
            metrics = {f"eval_{key}": val for key, val in metrics.items()}

        logs.update(metrics)
        super().log(logs, start_time)
        self._metrics[mode].clear()

        if self.accelerator.is_main_process and self.log_completions:
            if is_rich_available():
                print_prompt_completions_sample(

                    self._logs["completion"],
                    self._logs["rewards"],
                    self._logs["advantages"],

                    self.num_completions_to_print,
                    extra=dict(self._logs["extra"]),
                )

            logging_backends = []
            if self.args.report_to and "wandb" in self.args.report_to and wandb.run is not None:
                logging_backends.append(wandb)
            if self.args.report_to and "trackio" in self.args.report_to:

arguments.content:
"""Offline check for the repaired pending-metrics flush loop in TRL's GRPO/RLOO trainers.

Extracts the flush block verbatim from the trainer source file (via AST, so the tested
code is the shipped code, not a copy) and executes it against a simulated 2-rank world:
`gather_object` concatenates per-rank lists (accelerate flattens), `accelerator.gather`
concatenates per-rank scalars (all-gather semantics, same result on every rank).
Asserts:
  1. collective call counts are identical across ranks (the original crash);
  2. when only one rank logs a metric, BOTH ranks record that rank's value (no zero dilution);
  3. when both log, the value is the cross-rank mean;
  4. when no rank logs, neither rank issues a collective;
  5. the original variant is detected as desyncing (sanity check of the harness itself).
"""

import ast
import math
import sys

import torch


def extract_flush_block(path):
    """Return the source of the fixed flush loop: `gathered_names = ...` through
    `self._pending_metrics.clear()`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
                    and len(node.targets) == 1
                    and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
                    and node.targets[0].id == "gathered_names"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    return "\n".join(lines[node.lineno - 1 : node.end_lineno + 6])
    raise RuntimeError("fixed flush block not found in " + path)


def extract_original_block(path):
    """Return the source of the ORIGINAL (pre-repair) flush loop for the negative control:
    `for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):` through `self._pending_metrics.clear()`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.For)
                    and isinstance(node.iter, ast.Call)
                    and ast.unparse(node.iter.func) == "sorted"
                    and ast.unparse(node.iter.args[0]) == "self._pending_metrics"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    body_end = node.body[-1].end_lineno
                    # include the trailing clear()
                    return "\n".join(lines[node.lineno - 1 : body_end + 1])
    raise RuntimeError("original flush loop not found (fine if it was removed): " + path)


class RankState:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = pending           # dict name -> list of values logged this batch
        self.metrics = {}                # dict name -> list of flushed values
        self.clear_calls = 0
        self.gather_calls = []           # names this rank entered a gather for


class FakeAccelerator:
    def __init__(self, world, rank):
        self._world = world
        self._rank = rank

    def gather(self, tensor):
        # all-gather semantics: every rank receives every rank's scalar, in rank order
        self._world.gather_count[self._rank] += 1
        vals = []
        for rs in self._world.ranks:
            rs.accelerator._value = None  # mark consumed lazily below
        # each rank stashes its local tensor when the loop asks the accelerator for it
        self._world.local_tensors[self._rank] = tensor
        if self._rank == len(self._world.ranks) - 1:
            # last rank's call completes the collective: build the gathered view on all
            stacked = torch.stack(self._world.local_tensors)
            self._world.gathered = stacked
        return self._world.gathered


class World:
    """Simulates a world of ranks running the flush block in lock-step round-robin:
    each rank runs the whole block one at a time, but collectives only 'complete' for
    real when every rank has issued the corresponding one — enforced by the harness
    checking per-call-index parity in run_block()."""

    def __init__(self, n, block_src, pending_lists):
        self.n = n
        self.gather_object_calls = [0] * n
        self.ranks = []
        for i in range(n):
            rs = RankState(pending_lists[i])
            rs.accelerator = FakeAccelerator(self, i)
            self.ranks.append(rs)
        self.local_tensors = {}
        self.gathered = None
        self.gather_count = [0] * n
        # gather stub: accelerate's gather_object flattens per-rank lists
        self.block_src = block_src

    def gather_object(self, obj):
        i = self.current_rank
        self.gather_object_calls[i] += 1
        self._go_objs[i] = obj
        if all(v is not None for v in self._go_objs):
            flat = [x for lst in self._go_objs for x in lst]
            self._go_result = flat
            self._go_objs = [None] * self.n
        return self._go_result

    def run(self, mode="train"):
        self._go_objs = [None] * self.n
        self._go_result = None
        self.gather_object_calls = [0] * self.n
        self.gather_count = [0] * self.n
        for i, rs in enumerate(self.ranks):
            self.current_rank = i
            self.local_tensors = {}
            self.gathered = None
            ns = {
                "gather_object": self.gather_object,
                "torch": torch,
                "self": FakeTrainer(rs),
                "mode": mode,
                "device": torch.device("cpu"),
            }
            exec(self.block_src, ns)
        # collective parity: identical counts on every rank, per collective type
        assert len(set(self.gather_object_calls)) == 1, f"gather_object desync: {self.gather_object_calls}"
        assert len(set(self.gather_count)) == 1, f"gather desync: {self.gather_count}"
        return {i: rs.metrics for i, rs in enumerate(self.ranks)}


class FakeTrainer:
    def __init__(self, rank_state):
        self._rs = rank_state
        self._pending_metrics = rank_state.pending
        self._metrics = {"train": {}, "eval": {}}
        self.accelerator = rank_state.accelerator


def fake_metrics(self):
    return self._rs.metrics


# Route self._metrics[mode][name] appends to a dict-of-lists, mirroring defaultdict(list).
class _Metrics(dict):
    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


def patch_trainer_class():
    # FakeTrainer._metrics must behave like {"train": defaultdict(list)}: do it via
    # property-free wrapping — replace _Metrics into the trainer before each world runs.
    fake = FakeTrainer
    return fake


def make_trainer(rank_state):
    t = FakeTrainer(rank_state)
    t._metrics = {"train": _Metrics(), "eval": _Metrics()}
    return t


def run_case(name, path, n=2, pending_lists=None, expect=None, check_values=None):
    block = extract_flush_block(path)
    w = World(n, block, pending_lists)
    # fix: the block does self._pending_metrics.get(...) — pending dicts are plain dicts
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        rs.trainer = make_trainer(rs)
    # rerun rank loop with the real trainer objects (simplest: inline)
    w.run_with = None
    results = execute(w)
    print(f"[{name}] OK — metrics per rank: {results}")
    if check_values:
        check_values(results)
    return results


def execute(w):
    ns_gathered = {}
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        w.current_rank = i
        w.local_tensors = {}
        w.gathered = None
        ns = {
            "gather_object": w.gather_object,
            "torch": torch,
            "self": rs.trainer,
            "mode": "train",
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        # reset per-world stub state lazily
        exec(w.block_src, ns)
    assert len(set(w.gather_object_calls)) == 1, f"gather_object desync: {w.gather_object_calls}"
    assert len(set(w.gather_count)) == 1, f"gather desync: {w.gather_count}"
    return {i: dict(rs.trainer._metrics["train"]) for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks)}


def negative_control(path):
    """Run the ORIGINAL loop under the same lock-step harness and show rank 1 enters a
    gather-free path while rank 0 enters one — i.e. the collective-order mismatch."""
    try:
        block = extract_original_block(path)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(f"[negative control skipped] {e}")
        return
    # Simulate: only compare per-rank number of .gather() entries.
    w = World(2, block, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    # World.run would exec the ORIGINAL block, which references gather_object - absent there.
    # Instead, just statically count: original block issues one accelerator.gather per local
    # pending key when sorted() yields keys; compute analytically.
    r0 = len({"answer_parse_rate"})
    r1 = len({})
    assert r0 != r1
    print(f"[negative control] original loop: rank0 enters {r0} gather(s), rank1 enters {r1} — desync confirmed")


GRPO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py"
RLOO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/rloo_trainer.py"


def check(i, results, name, expected, rel=1e-6):
    for rank in range(len(results)):
        v = results[rank].get(name)
        assert v is not None, f"rank {rank} missing metric {name!r}"
        assert len(v) == 1, f"rank {rank} metric {name!r} has {len(v)} values"
        assert math.isclose(v[0], expected, rel_tol=rel), f"rank {rank} {name} = {v[0]} != {expected}"
        assert not math.isnan(v[0]), "value must not be NaN"


def main():
    block_g = extract_flush_block(GRPO)
    print("---- extracted GRPO block ----")
    print(block_g)
    print("------------------------------")

    # Same block must exist in RLOO
    block_r = extract_flush_block(RLOO)
    assert block_g.splitlines()[-1] == block_r.splitlines()[-1], "RLOO block tail differs"
    assert "gathered_names" in block_r, "RLOO not repaired?"

    # Case 1 (the staged failure): only rank 0 logs answer_parse_rate
    w = World(2, block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        rs.trainer = make_trainer(rs)
    res = execute(w)
    check(0, res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    print(f"case1 OK: {res}")

    # Case 2: both ranks log the same metric (.average across ranks)
    w = World(2, block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.6]}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.8]}])
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        rs.trainer = make_trainer(rs)
    res = execute(w)
    check(0, res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.7)
    print(f"case2 OK: {res}")

    # Case 3: only rank 1 logs it — the symmetric case
    w = World(2, block_g, [{}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.4]}])
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        rs.trainer = make_trainer(rs)
    res = execute(w)
    check(0, res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.4)
    print(f"case3 OK: {res}")

    # Case 4: nobody logs anything — zero collectives, metric absent everywhere
    w = World(2, block_g, [{}, {}])
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        rs.trainer = make_trainer(rs)

"""Offline check for the repaired pending-metrics flush loop in TRL's GRPO/RLOO trainers.

Extracts the flush block verbatim from the trainer source file (via AST, so the tested
code is the shipped code, not a copy) and executes it against a simulated 2-rank world:
`gather_object` concatenates per-rank lists (accelerate flattens), `accelerator.gather`
concatenates per-rank scalars (all-gather semantics, same result on every rank).
Asserts:
  1. collective call counts are identical across ranks (the original crash);
  2. when only one rank logs a metric, BOTH ranks record that rank's value (no zero dilution);
  3. when both log, the value is the cross-rank mean;
  4. when no rank logs, neither rank issues a collective;
  5. the original variant is detected as desyncing (sanity check of the harness itself).
"""

import ast
import math
import sys

import torch


def extract_flush_block(path):
    """Return the source of the fixed flush loop: `gathered_names = ...` through
    `self._pending_metrics.clear()`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
                    and len(node.targets) == 1
                    and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
                    and node.targets[0].id == "gathered_names"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    return "\n".join(lines[node.lineno - 1 : node.end_lineno + 6])
    raise RuntimeError("fixed flush block not found in " + path)


def extract_original_block(path):
    """Return the source of the ORIGINAL (pre-repair) flush loop for the negative control:
    `for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):` through `self._pending_metrics.clear()`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.For)
                    and isinstance(node.iter, ast.Call)
                    and ast.unparse(node.iter.func) == "sorted"
                    and ast.unparse(node.iter.args[0]) == "self._pending_metrics"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    body_end = node.body[-1].end_lineno
                    # include the trailing clear()
                    return "\n".join(lines[node.lineno - 1 : body_end + 1])
    raise RuntimeError("original flush loop not found (fine if it was removed): " + path)


class RankState:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = pending           # dict name -> list of values logged this batch
        self.metrics = {}                # dict name -> list of flushed values
        self.clear_calls = 0
        self.gather_calls = []           # names this rank entered a gather for


class FakeAccelerator:
    def __init__(self, world, rank):
        self._world = world
        self._rank = rank

    def gather(self, tensor):
        # all-gather semantics: every rank receives every rank's scalar, in rank order
        self._world.gather_count[self._rank] += 1
        vals = []
        for rs in self._world.ranks:
            rs.accelerator._value = None  # mark consumed lazily below
        # each rank stashes its local tensor when the loop asks the accelerator for it
        self._world.local_tensors[self._rank] = tensor
        if self._rank == len(self._world.ranks) - 1:
            # last rank's call completes the collective: build the gathered view on all
            stacked = torch.stack(self._world.local_tensors)
            self._world.gathered = stacked
        return self._world.gathered


class World:
    """Simulates a world of ranks running the flush block in lock-step round-robin:
    each rank runs the whole block one at a time, but collectives only 'complete' for
    real when every rank has issued the corresponding one — enforced by the harness
    checking per-call-index parity in run_block()."""

    def __init__(self, n, block_src, pending_lists):
        self.n = n
        self.gather_object_calls = [0] * n
        self.ranks = []
        for i in range(n):
            rs = RankState(pending_lists[i])
            rs.accelerator = FakeAccelerator(self, i)
            self.ranks.append(rs)
        self.local_tensors = {}
        self.gathered = None
        self.gather_count = [0] * n
        # gather stub: accelerate's gather_object flattens per-rank lists
        self.block_src = block_src

    def gather_object(self, obj):
        i = self.current_rank
        self.gather_object_calls[i] += 1
        self._go_objs[i] = obj
        if all(v is not None for v in self._go_objs):
            flat = [x for lst in self._go_objs for x in lst]
            self._go_result = flat
            self._go_objs = [None] * self.n
        return self._go_result

    def run(self, mode="train"):
        self._go_objs = [None] * self.n
        self._go_result = None
        self.gather_object_calls = [0] * self.n
        self.gather_count = [0] * self.n
        for i, rs in enumerate(self.ranks):
            self.current_rank = i
            self.local_tensors = {}
            self.gathered = None
            ns = {
                "gather_object": self.gather_object,
                "torch": torch,
                "self": FakeTrainer(rs),
                "mode": mode,
                "device": torch.device("cpu"),
            }
            exec(self.block_src, ns)
        # collective parity: identical counts on every rank, per collective type
        assert len(set(self.gather_object_calls)) == 1, f"gather_object desync: {self.gather_object_calls}"
        assert len(set(self.gather_count)) == 1, f"gather desync: {self.gather_count}"
        return {i: rs.metrics for i, rs in enumerate(self.ranks)}


class FakeTrainer:
    def __init__(self, rank_state):
        self._rs = rank_state
        self._pending_metrics = rank_state.pending
        self._metrics = {"train": {}, "eval": {}}
        self.accelerator = rank_state.accelerator


def fake_metrics(self):
    return self._rs.metrics


# Route self._metrics[mode][name] appends to a dict-of-lists, mirroring defaultdict(list).
class _Metrics(dict):
    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


def patch_trainer_class():
    # FakeTrainer._metrics must behave like {"train": defaultdict(list)}: do it via
    # property-free wrapping — replace _Metrics into the trainer before each world runs.
    fake = FakeTrainer
    return fake


def make_trainer(rank_state):
    t = FakeTrainer(rank_state)
    t._metrics = {"train": _Metrics(), "eval": _Metrics()}
    return t


def run_case(name, path, n=2, pending_lists=None, expect=None, check_values=None):
    block = extract_flush_block(path)
    w = World(n, block, pending_lists)
    # fix: the block does self._pending_metrics.get(...) — pending dicts are plain dicts
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        rs.trainer = make_trainer(rs)
    # rerun rank loop with the real trainer objects (simplest: inline)
    w.run_with = None
    results = execute(w)
    print(f"[{name}] OK — metrics per rank: {results}")
    if check_values:
        check_values(results)
    return results


def execute(w):
    ns_gathered = {}
    for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks):
        w.current_rank = i
        w.local_tensors = {}
        w.gathered = None
        ns = {
            "gather_object": w.gather_object,
            "torch": torch,
            "self": rs.trainer,
            "mode": "train",
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        # reset per-world stub state lazily
        exec(w.block_src, ns)
    assert len(set(w.gather_object_calls)) == 1, f"gather_object desync: {w.gather_object_calls}"
    assert len(set(w.gather_count)) == 1, f"gather desync: {w.gather_count}"
    return {i: dict(rs.trainer._metrics["train"]) for i, rs in enumerate(w.ranks)}


def negative_control(path):
    """Run the ORIGINAL loop under the same lock-step harness and show rank 1 enters a
    gather-free path while rank 0 enters one — i.e. the collective-order mismatch."""
    try:
        block = extract_original_block(path)
    except RuntimeError as e:

# Instead of returning a standard per-step batch (i.e., `per_device_batch_size), our dataloader loads an
    # *generation* batch (i.e., `per_device_batch_size × steps_per_generation`). This allows us to generate completions
    # once every steps_per_generation step—rather than once per accumulation step—which is significantly more
    # efficient. Thus, `_prepare_inputs` is called with this *generation* batch, and it handles the splitting internally.
    # Maintenance note: this method is a copy-paste of the original `Trainer.get_train_dataloader` with two changes: the
    # batch size is multiplied by `steps_per_generation`, and iterable datasets are wrapped (see `repeat_iterable_dataset`).
    def get_train_dataloader(self):
        dataset = self.train_dataset
        if isinstance(dataset, IterableDataset):
            # Iterable datasets can't be indexed, so RepeatSampler can't be attached. Reproduce its ordering by
            # transforming the stream instead (see `repeat_iterable_dataset`). The full permutation done by
            # RepeatSampler becomes a buffered shuffle here.
            if self.shuffle_dataset:
                dataset = dataset.shuffle(seed=self.args.seed)
            dataset = repeat_iterable_dataset(
                dataset,
                mini_repeat_count=self.num_generations,
                batch_size=self.args.generation_batch_size // self.num_generations,
                repeat_count=self.num_iterations * self.args.steps_per_generation,
            )
        return self._get_dataloader(
            dataset=dataset,
            description="Training",
            batch_size=self._train_batch_size * self.args.steps_per_generation,  # < this is the change
            sampler_fn=self._get_train_sampler,
            is_training=True,
        )

    def _get_train_sampler(self, dataset: Dataset | None = None) -> Sampler:
        # Returns a sampler that
        # 1. ensures each prompt is repeated across multiple processes. This guarantees that identical prompts are
        #    distributed to different GPUs, allowing rewards to be computed and normalized correctly within each prompt
        #    group. Using the same seed across processes ensures consistent prompt assignment, preventing discrepancies
        #    in group formation.
        # 2. repeats the batch multiple times to allow reusing generations across multiple updates. Refer to
        #    _prepare_inputs to see how the generations are stored and reused.

        # In the following figure, the values are the prompt indices. Each row shows the per-step batch
        # returned by `_prepare_inputs`; rows within a `steps_per_generation` block are slices of the same
        # generated batch. When `num_iterations > 1`, that block is reused for multiple optimization passes
        # before regenerating.
        #
        #                                      |   GPU 0  |   GPU 1  |

steps.message: The script I drafted got tangled mid-write — rewriting it cleanly with a two-pass collective stub (pass 1 records each rank's inputs, pass 2 returns the true all-gathered stack, so the real `.nanmean()` arithmetic runs on the actual extracted code):
steps.reasoning_content:
That test script got convoluted mid-write (leftover dead functions like `run_case`, `patch_trainer_class`, `fake_metrics`, and the World/FakeAccelerator split is awkward). Let me simplify it to a clean, correct script. The key mechanics:

- `gather_object(obj)` stub: each rank calls it with its local list; the collective "completes" only when all ranks have issued it; returns flattened list to every rank.
- `accelerator.gather(t)` stub: same — completes when all ranks issued; returns stacked tensor to every rank.
- The block references `self.accelerator.gather`, `self._pending_metrics`, `self._metrics[mode]`, plus free names `gather_object`, `torch`, `mode`, `device`.

A simple correct approach: simulate "lock-step" by running each rank's block to completion sequentially is wrong for collective semantics (a real desync would deadlock, not mis-order). But for a logic test, sequential execution with completion-on-all-called is fine IF I model the collectives as blocking: each rank's `gather` call "blocks" until all ranks reached the same call index. I can implement blocking via a simple rendezvous: since I'm running ranks in one thread, I can't actually block. 

Cleaner: run the two ranks as real concurrent processes? Overkill. 

Alternative that still validates the important properties without simulating blocking:
1. **Value correctness** (union, NaN-aware mean, no zero dilution): run each rank's block in isolation, stubbing `gather_object` to return the world-flattened list and `accelerator.gather` to return the world-stacked tensor. This checks the arithmetic and the union logic — the properties the verifier cares about (both ranks log supplier's value).
2. **Collective parity** (the crash): statically verify every rank executes the same *number* of `accelerator.gather` and `gather_object` calls given the flattened world — which follows structurally since every rank iterates the same sorted set of names. I can assert: per-rank call counts equal number of unioned names + 1, and identical across ranks.

For the negative control (original code), the same isolation-based stubs don't detect desync — but I can statically count: original loop iterates over LOCAL pending names, so rank0 → 1 gather, rank1 → 0 gathers. I can extract the original block… wait, the original block no longer exists in the file (I replaced it). I'd have to reconstruct it from git… there's no git repo. I have the original text in the summary and in my Edit call. I can embed the original snippet in the test as a string for the negative control. That's acceptable — it's a control demonstrating the harness catches divergence, using the pre-repair code I recorded.

Actually, the cleanest demonstration of the desync: run the ORIGINAL block with a rendezvous-based stub that only completes a collective when all ranks issued the same-index call — with per-rank execution in lock-step *statement by statement*? That's over-engineering.

Simpler rendezvous: execute rank 0's block fully, but make each collective call record (kind, index) and require that when rank 1's block runs, its collective sequence matches rank 0's exactly. If rank 1 issues a different number/kinds of collectives, the check fails — which is precisely the mismatch NCCL detected. It's a valid model of "same collective sequence" without true blocking. 

So: `gather_object` and `accelerator.gather` stubs append to `seq[rank]`; after both ranks run, assert `seq[0] == seq[1]`. With the original code: rank0 seq = [("go",0),("g",0)], rank1 seq = [("go",0)] → mismatch → detected. With the fix: both equal. 

Let me rewrite the script cleanly with this model:

```python
class Rank:
    def __init__(self, world, idx, pending):
        self.world = world; self.idx = idx
        self.pending = pending
        self.metrics = {}  # dict-of-lists via _Metrics
        self.accelerator = FakeAccel(world, idx)
```

collective stubs live on `world`:
```python
class World:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.seq = [[] for _ in range(n)]      # collective call sequences per rank
        self.go_inputs = [None]*n              # latest gather_object args per rank
        self.g_inputs = [None]*n
    def gather_object(self, obj):
        w = self
        i = w.current
        w.seq[i].append(("gather_object", len(w.seq[i])))
        w.go_inputs[i] = obj
        if all(x is not None for x in w.go_inputs):
            flat = [x for lst in w.go_inputs for x in lst]  # accelerate flattens
            w.go_result = flat
            w.go_inputs = [None]*w.n
        return w.go_result
```
Hmm — but with sequential execution: rank 0 runs the whole block first; its first `gather_object` call: not all ranks have issued yet (`go_inputs[1] is None`) → `w.go_result` stays None → returns None → rank 0's `gathered_names = None` → `set(None)` → TypeError!

To handle sequential execution, the stub must return the correct result immediately. Precompute: since I know all ranks' pending dicts upfront, `gather_object` can compute the flattened result from the world's pending lists directly (the "collective" result), and just record the sequence. Same for `gather`: to return the stacked tensor, it needs all ranks' local tensors — but with sequential execution, rank 1 hasn't produced its tensor yet.

Options: (a) run ranks interleaved per-statement — too complex; (b) make gather return a lazily-computed value — the block calls `.nanmean().item()` immediately, so no; (c) two-pass: run each rank twice — first pass records each rank's local tensor per call index; second pass returns the stacked result. That works! The collective inputs are deterministic given the world state (rank's pending metrics + gathered names — both independent of the gather results... wait, is the *number* of gathers independent? """Offline check for the repaired pending-metrics flush loop in TRL's GRPO/RLOO trainers.

Extracts the flush block verbatim from the trainer source (via AST, so the tested code is
the shipped code, not a copy) and executes it for a simulated 2-rank world:

  * `gather_object(obj)` mirrors accelerate.utils.gather_object: every rank calls it with
    its local list, every rank receives the flat concatenation of all ranks' lists.
  * `accelerator.gather(t)` mirrors Accelerator.gather: every rank receives the stack of
    all ranks' tensors. Because ranks are executed sequentially here, this needs two
    passes: pass 1 records each rank's local tensor per collective call index, pass 2
    replays the block returning the true stacked result so the real nanmean arithmetic
    runs on the real code.

Assertions:
  1. every rank issues the identical sequence of collectives (the original crash);
  2. when only one rank logs a metric, BOTH ranks record exactly that rank's value
     (no zero dilution, no NaN);
  3. when both ranks log, the value is the cross-rank mean;
  4. when nobody logs, no `accelerator.gather` is issued on any rank;
  5. multiple values logged by a rank are averaged locally first;
  6. the pre-repair loop (embedded below as the negative control) fails assertion 1.
"""

import ast
import math

import torch

GRPO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py"
RLOO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/rloo_trainer.py"

ORIGINAL_BLOCK = """\
        for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):
            values = self._pending_metrics[name]
            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item()
            self._metrics[mode][name].append(global_mean)
        self._pending_metrics.clear()
"""


def extract_flush_block(path):
    """Return the source of the repaired flush block: `gathered_names = ...` through
    `self._pending_metrics.clear()`, from inside `_generate_and_score_completions`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
                    and len(node.targets) == 1
                    and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
                    and node.targets[0].id == "gathered_names"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    start = node.lineno - 1
                    end = next(j for j in range(start, start + 20) if "_pending_metrics.clear()" in lines[j]) + 1
                    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])
    raise RuntimeError(f"repaired flush block not found in {path}")


class _Metrics(dict):
    """dict-of-lists behaving like defaultdict(list)."""

    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


class Rank:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = dict(pending)
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.go_calls = []    # args passed to gather_object, in call order
        self.g_calls = []     # local tensors passed to accelerator.gather, in call order
        self.g_results = []   # tensors returned by accelerator.gather, in call order

    def fresh(self):
        """Reset state accumulated during the recording pass."""
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.g_results = []
        return self


class RecordingAccelerator:
    """Pass-1 accelerator: records the local tensor, returns a placeholder of the shape
    the real gather would return (world_size,). Values appended this pass are discarded."""

    def __init__(self, rank, world_size):
        self._rank, self._world_size = rank, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        return torch.zeros(self._world_size, dtype=tensor.dtype)


class ReplayAccelerator:
    """Pass-2 accelerator: returns the true all-gathered stack for this call index."""

    def __init__(self, rank, recorded, world_size):
        self._rank, self._recorded, self._world_size = rank, recorded, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        stack = torch.stack([r.g_calls[len(self._rank.g_results)] for r in self._recorded])
        assert stack.shape == (self._world_size,), stack.shape
        return stack


def run_world(block, pending_lists, mode="train"):
    """Execute `block` once per rank against collective stubs; return per-rank metrics.

    Pass 1 records each rank's local tensors; pass 2 replays with true stacked results
    so the code under test performs its own nanmean/append on real gathered values.
    """
    ranks = [Rank(p) for p in pending_lists]
    n = len(ranks)

    # Pass 1: record what each rank would hand to each collective.
    for r in ranks:
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: (r.go_calls.append(obj), [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst])[1],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r, RecordingAccelerator(r, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    # Every rank must have passed its own sorted key list to gather_object.
    for r, pending in zip(ranks, pending_lists):
        assert r.go_calls == [sorted(pending)], (r.go_calls, sorted(pending))
    # Every rank must issue the same number of gathers (same name union → same count).
    counts = [len(r.g_calls) for r in ranks]
    assert len(set(counts)) == 1, f"accelerator.gather desync: {counts}"

    # Pass 2: replay with the true stacked tensors.
    for r in ranks:
        r2 = r.fresh()
        r._replay = r2
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r2, ReplayAccelerator(r2, ranks, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    return {i: dict(r._replay.metrics) for i, r in enumerate(ranks)}, counts


class SimpleTrainer:
    """Just the attributes the flush block touches."""

    def __init__(self, rank, accelerator):
        self._pending_metrics = rank.pending
        self._metrics = {"train": rank.metrics, "eval": _Metrics()}
        self.accelerator = accelerator


def expect(results, name, value, per_rank=None):
    for rank, metrics in results.items():
        vals = metrics.get(name)
        assert vals is not None, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} missing from {metrics}"
        assert len(vals) == 1, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} appended {len(vals)} times"
        v = vals[0]
        assert not math.isnan(v), f"rank {rank}: {name} is NaN"
        expected = per_rank[rank] if per_rank else value
        assert math.isclose(v, expected, rel_tol=1e-6), f"rank {rank}: {name} = {v}, expected {expected}"


def main():
    block_g = extract_flush_block(GRPO)
    block_r = extract_flush_block(RLOO)
    print("---- repaired GRPO block ----")
    print(block_g)
    print("-----------------------------")
    compile(block_g, GRPO, "exec")
    compile(block_r, RLOO, "exec")
    # GRPO and RLOO must carry the identical repair.
    assert block_g.strip() == block_r.strip(), "GRPO and RLOO flush blocks differ"

    # Case 1 — the staged failure: only rank 0 logs answer_parse_rate.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    assert counts == [1, 1], counts
    print(f"case 1 OK  (only rank 0 logs): {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 2 — both ranks log: cross-rank mean.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.6]}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.8]}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.7)
    print(f"case 2 OK  (both log, mean):   {res}")

    # Case 3 — only rank 1 logs (symmetric).
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.4]}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.4)
    print(f"case 3 OK  (only rank 1 logs): {res}")

    # Case 4 — nobody logs: no gather issued anywhere, no metric fabricated.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{}, {}])
    assert res == {0: {}, 1: {}}, res
    assert counts == [0, 0], counts
    print(f"case 4 OK  (nobody logs):      {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 5 — disjoint names across ranks: union logged everywhere, same order.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"a_metric": [1.0], "z_metric": [2.0]}, {"m_metric": [3.0]}])
    for rank, metrics in res.items():
        assert sorted(metrics) == ["a_metric", "m_metric", "z_metric"], metrics
    expect(res, "a_metric", 1.0)
    expect(res, "m_metric", 3.0)
    expect(res, "z_metric", 2.0)
    assert counts == [3, 3], counts
    print(f"case 5 OK  (disjoint names):   {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 6 — a rank logging several values per batch: averaged locally, then gathered.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.5, 1.0, 0.25]}, {}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    print(f"case 6 OK  (multi-value mean): {res}")

    # Negative control — the pre-repair loop desyncs the collectives.
    try:
        run_world(ORIGINAL_BLOCK, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"negative control OK (pre-repair loop detected): {e}")
    else:
        raise SystemExit("negative control FAILED: original loop was not detected as desyncing")
    # ...and it logged the metric on rank 0 only (the other failure mode).
    res_orig, _ = run_world(ORIGINAL_BLOCK.replace("self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device))", "torch.ones(2)"), [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    assert "answer_parse_rate" in res_orig[0] and "answer_parse_rate" not in res_orig[1], res_orig
    print(f"negative control OK (rank 0 only logged it): {res_orig}")

    print("\nALL CHECKS PASSED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  * `accelerator.gather(t)` mirrors Accelerator.gather: every rank receives the stack of
    all ranks' tensors. Because ranks are executed sequentially here, this needs two
    passes: pass 1 records each rank's local tensor per collective call index, pass 2
    replays the block returning the true stacked result so the real nanmean arithmetic
    runs on the real code.

Assertions:
  1. every rank issues the identical sequence of collectives (the original crash);
  2. when only one rank logs a metric, BOTH ranks record exactly that rank's value
     (no zero dilution, no NaN);
  3. when both ranks log, the value is the cross-rank mean;
  4. when nobody logs, no `accelerator.gather` is issued on any rank;
  5. multiple values logged by a rank are averaged locally first;
  6. the pre-repair loop (embedded below as the negative control) fails assertion 1.
"""

import ast
import math

import torch

GRPO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py"
RLOO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/rloo_trainer.py"

ORIGINAL_BLOCK = """\
        for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):
            values = self._pending_metrics[name]
            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item()
            self._metrics[mode][name].append(global_mean)
        self._pending_metrics.clear()
"""


def extract_flush_block(path):
    """Return the source of the repaired flush block: `gathered_names = ...` through
    `self._pending_metrics.clear()`, from inside `_generate_and_score_completions`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
                    and len(node.targets) == 1
                    and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
                    and node.targets[0].id == "gathered_names"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    start = node.lineno - 1
                    end = next(j for j in range(start, start + 20) if "_pending_metrics.clear()" in lines[j]) + 1
                    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])
    raise RuntimeError(f"repaired flush block not found in {path}")


class _Metrics(dict):
    """dict-of-lists behaving like defaultdict(list)."""

    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


class Rank:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = dict(pending)
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.go_calls = []    # args passed to gather_object, in call order
        self.g_calls = []     # local tensors passed to accelerator.gather, in call order
        self.g_results = []   # tensors returned by accelerator.gather, in call order

    def fresh(self):
        """Reset state accumulated during the recording pass."""
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.g_results = []
        return self


class RecordingAccelerator:
    """Pass-1 accelerator: records the local tensor, returns a placeholder of the shape
    the real gather would return (world_size,). Values appended this pass are discarded."""

    def __init__(self, rank, world_size):
        self._rank, self._world_size = rank, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        return torch.zeros(self._world_size, dtype=tensor.dtype)


class ReplayAccelerator:
    """Pass-2 accelerator: returns the true all-gathered stack for this call index."""

    def __init__(self, rank, recorded, world_size):
        self._rank, self._recorded, self._world_size = rank, recorded, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        stack = torch.stack([r.g_calls[len(self._rank.g_results)] for r in self._recorded])
        assert stack.shape == (self._world_size,), stack.shape
        return stack


def run_world(block, pending_lists, mode="train"):
    """Execute `block` once per rank against collective stubs; return per-rank metrics.

    Pass 1 records each rank's local tensors; pass 2 replays with true stacked results
    so the code under test performs its own nanmean/append on real gathered values.
    """
    ranks = [Rank(p) for p in pending_lists]
    n = len(ranks)

    # Pass 1: record what each rank would hand to each collective.
    for r in ranks:
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: (r.go_calls.append(obj), [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst])[1],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r, RecordingAccelerator(r, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    # Every rank must have passed its own sorted key list to gather_object.
    for r, pending in zip(ranks, pending_lists):
        assert r.go_calls == [sorted(pending)], (r.go_calls, sorted(pending))
    # Every rank must issue the same number of gathers (same name union → same count).
    counts = [len(r.g_calls) for r in ranks]
    assert len(set(counts)) == 1, f"accelerator.gather desync: {counts}"

    # Pass 2: replay with the true stacked tensors.
    for r in ranks:
        r2 = r.fresh()
        r._replay = r2
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r2, ReplayAccelerator(r2, ranks, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    return {i: dict(r._replay.metrics) for i, r in enumerate(ranks)}, counts


class SimpleTrainer:
    """Just the attributes the flush block touches."""

    def __init__(self, rank, accelerator):
        self._pending_metrics = rank.pending
        self._metrics = {"train": rank.metrics, "eval": _Metrics()}
        self.accelerator = accelerator


def expect(results, name, value, per_rank=None):
    for rank, metrics in results.items():
        vals = metrics.get(name)
        assert vals is not None, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} missing from {metrics}"
        assert len(vals) == 1, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} appended {len(vals)} times"
        v = vals[0]
        assert not math.isnan(v), f"rank {rank}: {name} is NaN"
        expected = per_rank[rank] if per_rank else value
        assert math.isclose(v, expected, rel_tol=1e-6), f"rank {rank}: {name} = {v}, expected {expected}"


def main():
    block_g = extract_flush_block(GRPO)
    block_r = extract_flush_block(RLOO)
    print("---- repaired GRPO block ----")
    print(block_g)
    print("-----------------------------")
    compile(block_g, GRPO, "exec")
    compile(block_r, RLOO, "exec")
    # GRPO and RLOO must carry the identical repair.
    assert block_g.strip() == block_r.strip(), "GRPO and RLOO flush blocks differ"

    # Case 1 — the staged failure: only rank 0 logs answer_parse_rate.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    assert counts == [1, 1], counts
    print(f"case 1 OK  (only rank 0 logs): {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 2 — both ranks log: cross-rank mean.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.6]}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.8]}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.7)
    print(f"case 2 OK  (both log, mean):   {res}")

    # Case 3 — only rank 1 logs (symmetric).
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.4]}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.4)
    print(f"case 3 OK  (only rank 1 logs): {res}")

    # Case 4 — nobody logs: no gather issued anywhere, no metric fabricated.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{}, {}])
    assert res == {0: {}, 1: {}}, res
    assert counts == [0, 0], counts
    print(f"case 4 OK  (nobody logs):      {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 5 — disjoint names across ranks: union logged everywhere, same order.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"a_metric": [1.0], "z_metric": [2.0]}, {"m_metric": [3.0]}])
    for rank, metrics in res.items():
        assert sorted(metrics) == ["a_metric", "m_metric", "z_metric"], metrics
    expect(res, "a_metric", 1.0)
    expect(res, "m_metric", 3.0)
    expect(res, "z_metric", 2.0)
    assert counts == [3, 3], counts
    print(f"case 5 OK  (disjoint names):   {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 6 — a rank logging several values per batch: averaged locally, then gathered.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.5, 1.0, 0.25]}, {}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    print(f"case 6 OK  (multi-value mean): {res}")

    # Negative control — the pre-repair loop desyncs the collectives.
    try:
        run_world(ORIGINAL_BLOCK, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"negative control OK (pre-repair loop detected): {e}")
    else:
        raise SystemExit("negative control FAILED: original loop was not detected as desyncing")
    # ...and it logged the metric on rank 0 only (the other failure mode).
    res_orig, _ = run_world(ORIGINAL_BLOCK.replace("self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device))", "torch.ones(2)"), [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    assert "answer_parse_rate" in res_orig[0] and "answer_parse_rate" not in res_orig[1], res_orig
    print(f"negative control OK (rank 0 only logged it): {res_orig}")

    print("\nALL CHECKS PASSED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Offline check for the repaired pending-metrics flush loop in TRL's GRPO/RLOO trainers.

Extracts the flush block verbatim from the trainer source (via AST, so the tested code is
the shipped code, not a copy) and executes it for a simulated 2-rank world:

  * `gather_object(obj)` mirrors accelerate.utils.gather_object: every rank calls it with
    its local list, every rank receives the flat concatenation of all ranks' lists.
  * `accelerator.gather(t)` mirrors Accelerator.gather: every rank receives the stack of
    all ranks' tensors. Because ranks are executed sequentially here, this needs two
    passes: pass 1 records each rank's local tensor per collective call index, pass 2
    replays the block returning the true stacked result so the real nanmean arithmetic
    runs on the real code.

Assertions:
  1. every rank issues the identical sequence of collectives (the original crash);
  2. when only one rank logs a metric, BOTH ranks record exactly that rank's value
     (no zero dilution, no NaN);
  3. when both ranks log, the value is the cross-rank mean;
  4. when nobody logs, no `accelerator.gather` is issued on any rank;
  5. multiple values logged by a rank are averaged locally first;
  6. the pre-repair loop (embedded below as the negative control) fails assertion 1.
"""

import ast
import math

import torch

GRPO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py"
RLOO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/rloo_trainer.py"

ORIGINAL_BLOCK = """\
        for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):
            values = self._pending_metrics[name]
            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item()
            self._metrics[mode][name].append(global_mean)
        self._pending_metrics.clear()
"""


def extract_flush_block(path):
    """Return the source of the repaired flush block: `gathered_names = ...` through
    `self._pending_metrics.clear()`, from inside `_generate_and_score_completions`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
                    and len(node.targets) == 1
                    and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
                    and node.targets[0].id == "gathered_names"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    start = node.lineno - 1
                    end = next(j for j in range(start, start + 20) if "_pending_metrics.clear()" in lines[j]) + 1
                    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])
    raise RuntimeError(f"repaired flush block not found in {path}")


class _Metrics(dict):
    """dict-of-lists behaving like defaultdict(list)."""

    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


class Rank:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = dict(pending)
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.go_calls = []    # args passed to gather_object, in call order
        self.g_calls = []     # local tensors passed to accelerator.gather, in call order
        self.g_results = []   # tensors returned by accelerator.gather, in call order

    def fresh(self):
        """Reset state accumulated during the recording pass."""
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.g_results = []
        return self


class RecordingAccelerator:
    """Pass-1 accelerator: records the local tensor, returns a placeholder of the shape
    the real gather would return (world_size,). Values appended this pass are discarded."""

    def __init__(self, rank, world_size):
        self._rank, self._world_size = rank, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        return torch.zeros(self._world_size, dtype=tensor.dtype)


class ReplayAccelerator:
    """Pass-2 accelerator: returns the true all-gathered stack for this call index."""

    def __init__(self, rank, recorded, world_size):
        self._rank, self._recorded, self._world_size = rank, recorded, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        stack = torch.stack([r.g_calls[len(self._rank.g_results)] for r in self._recorded])
        assert stack.shape == (self._world_size,), stack.shape
        return stack


def run_world(block, pending_lists, mode="train"):
    """Execute `block` once per rank against collective stubs; return per-rank metrics.

    Pass 1 records each rank's local tensors; pass 2 replays with true stacked results
    so the code under test performs its own nanmean/append on real gathered values.
    """
    ranks = [Rank(p) for p in pending_lists]
    n = len(ranks)

    # Pass 1: record what each rank would hand to each collective.
    for r in ranks:
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: (r.go_calls.append(obj), [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst])[1],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r, RecordingAccelerator(r, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    # Every rank must have passed its own sorted key list to gather_object.
    for r, pending in zip(ranks, pending_lists):
        assert r.go_calls == [sorted(pending)], (r.go_calls, sorted(pending))
    # Every rank must issue the same number of gathers (same name union → same count).
    counts = [len(r.g_calls) for r in ranks]
    assert len(set(counts)) == 1, f"accelerator.gather desync: {counts}"

    # Pass 2: replay with the true stacked tensors.
    for r in ranks:
        r2 = r.fresh()
        r._replay = r2
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r2, ReplayAccelerator(r2, ranks, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    return {i: dict(r._replay.metrics) for i, r in enumerate(ranks)}, counts


class SimpleTrainer:
    """Just the attributes the flush block touches."""

    def __init__(self, rank, accelerator):
        self._pending_metrics = rank.pending
        self._metrics = {"train": rank.metrics, "eval": _Metrics()}
        self.accelerator = accelerator


def expect(results, name, value, per_rank=None):
    for rank, metrics in results.items():
        vals = metrics.get(name)
        assert vals is not None, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} missing from {metrics}"
        assert len(vals) == 1, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} appended {len(vals)} times"
        v = vals[0]
        assert not math.isnan(v), f"rank {rank}: {name} is NaN"
        expected = per_rank[rank] if per_rank else value
        assert math.isclose(v, expected, rel_tol=1e-6), f"rank {rank}: {name} = {v}, expected {expected}"


def main():
    block_g = extract_flush_block(GRPO)
    block_r = extract_flush_block(RLOO)
    print("---- repaired GRPO block ----")
    print(block_g)
    print("-----------------------------")
    compile(block_g, GRPO, "exec")
    compile(block_r, RLOO, "exec")
    # GRPO and RLOO must carry the identical repair.
    assert block_g.strip() == block_r.strip(), "GRPO and RLOO flush blocks differ"

    # Case 1 — the staged failure: only rank 0 logs answer_parse_rate.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    assert counts == [1, 1], counts
    print(f"case 1 OK  (only rank 0 logs): {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 2 — both ranks log: cross-rank mean.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.6]}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.8]}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.7)
    print(f"case 2 OK  (both log, mean):   {res}")

    # Case 3 — only rank 1 logs (symmetric).
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{}, {"answer_parse_rate": [0.4]}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.4)
    print(f"case 3 OK  (only rank 1 logs): {res}")

    # Case 4 — nobody logs: no gather issued anywhere, no metric fabricated.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{}, {}])
    assert res == {0: {}, 1: {}}, res
    assert counts == [0, 0], counts
    print(f"case 4 OK  (nobody logs):      {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 5 — disjoint names across ranks: union logged everywhere, same order.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"a_metric": [1.0], "z_metric": [2.0]}, {"m_metric": [3.0]}])
    for rank, metrics in res.items():
        assert sorted(metrics) == ["a_metric", "m_metric", "z_metric"], metrics
    expect(res, "a_metric", 1.0)
    expect(res, "m_metric", 3.0)
    expect(res, "z_metric", 2.0)
    assert counts == [3, 3], counts
    print(f"case 5 OK  (disjoint names):   {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    # Case 6 — a rank logging several values per batch: averaged locally, then gathered.
    res, counts = run_world(block_g, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.5, 1.0, 0.25]}, {}])
    expect(res, "answer_parse_rate", 0.75)
    print(f"case 6 OK  (multi-value mean): {res}")

    # Negative control — the pre-repair loop desyncs the collectives.
    try:
        run_world(ORIGINAL_BLOCK, [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"negative control OK (pre-repair loop detected): {e}")
    else:
        raise SystemExit("negative control FAILED: original loop was not detected as desyncing")
    # ...and it logged the metric on rank 0 only (the other failure mode).
    res_orig, _ = run_world(ORIGINAL_BLOCK.replace("self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device))", "torch.ones(2)"), [{"answer_parse_rate": [0.75]}, {}])
    assert "answer_parse_rate" in res_orig[0] and "answer_parse_rate" not in res_orig[1], res_orig
    print(f"negative control OK (rank 0 only logged it): {res_orig}")

    print("\nALL CHECKS PASSED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```python
class RepeatSampler(Sampler):
    def __init__(
        self,
        data_source: Sized,
        mini_repeat_count: int,
        batch_size: int = 1,
        repeat_count: int = 1,
        shuffle: bool = True,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        self.data_source = data_source
        self.mini_repeat_count = mini_repeat_count
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.repeat_count = repeat_count
        self.num_samples = len(data_source)
        self.shuffle = shuffle
        self.seed = seed

        if shuffle:
            self.generator = torch.Generator()  # Create a local random generator
            if seed is not None:
                self.generator.manual_seed(seed)

    def __iter__(self):
        if self.shuffle:
            indexes = torch.randperm(self.num_samples, generator=self.generator).tolist()
        else:
            indexes = list(range(self.num_samples))
        # e.g. [2, 4, 3, 1, 0, 6, 5] (num_samples = 7)
        # -> [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [5]] (batch_size = 3)
        indexes = [indexes[i : i + self.batch_size] for i in range(0, len(indexes), self.batch_size)]
        # e.g. [[2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [5]] -> repeat_count=2
        # -> [[2, 4, 3], [2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [1, 0, 6], [5], [5]]
        indexes = [chunk for chunk in indexes for _ in range(self.repeat_count)]
        # e.g. [[2, 4, 3], [2, 4, 3], [1, 0, 6], [1, 0, 6], [5], [5]] -> mini_repeat_count=3
        # -> [2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, ...]
        for chunk in indexes:
            for index in chunk:
                for _ in range(self.mini_repeat_count):
                    yield index

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return (self.num_samples // self.batch_size) * self.batch_size * self.mini_repeat_count * self.repeat_count
```

  2. when only one rank logs a metric, BOTH ranks record exactly that rank's value

  3. when both ranks log, the value is the cross-rank mean;
  4. when nobody logs, no `accelerator.gather` is issued on any rank;
  5. multiple values logged by a rank are averaged locally first;
  6. the pre-repair loop (embedded below as the negative control) fails assertion 1.

import ast
import math

import torch

GRPO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py"
RLOO = "/workspace/src/trl/trainer/rloo_trainer.py"

ORIGINAL_BLOCK = """\
        for name in sorted(self._pending_metrics):
            values = self._pending_metrics[name]
            local_mean = sum(values) / len(values)
            global_mean = self.accelerator.gather(torch.tensor(local_mean, device=device)).mean().item()

        self._pending_metrics.clear()

def extract_flush_block(path):
    """Return the source of the repaired flush block: `gathered_names = ...` through
    `self._pending_metrics.clear()`, from inside `_generate_and_score_completions`."""
    src = open(path).read()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for fn in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(fn, ast.FunctionDef) and fn.name == "_generate_and_score_completions":
            for node in ast.walk(fn):
                if (
                    isinstance(node, ast.Assign)
                    and len(node.targets) == 1
                    and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
                    and node.targets[0].id == "gathered_names"
                ):
                    lines = src.splitlines()
                    start = node.lineno - 1
                    end = next(j for j in range(start, start + 20) if "_pending_metrics.clear()" in lines[j]) + 1
                    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])
    raise RuntimeError(f"repaired flush block not found in {path}")


class _Metrics(dict):
    """dict-of-lists behaving like defaultdict(list)."""

    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


class Rank:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = dict(pending)
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.go_calls = []    # args passed to gather_object, in call order
        self.g_calls = []     # local tensors passed to accelerator.gather, in call order
        self.g_results = []   # tensors returned by accelerator.gather, in call order

    def fresh(self):
        """Reset state accumulated during the recording pass."""
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.g_results = []
        return self


class RecordingAccelerator:
    """Pass-1 accelerator: records the local tensor, returns a placeholder of the shape
    the real gather would return (world_size,). Values appended this pass are discarded."""

    def __init__(self, rank, world_size):
        self._rank, self._world_size = rank, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        return torch.zeros(self._world_size, dtype=tensor.dtype)


class ReplayAccelerator:
    """Pass-2 accelerator: returns the true all-gathered stack for this call index."""

    def __init__(self, rank, recorded, world_size):
        self._rank, self._recorded, self._world_size = rank, recorded, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        stack = torch.stack([r.g_calls[len(self._rank.g_results)] for r in self._recorded])

    """Execute `block` once per rank against collective stubs; return per-rank metrics.

    Pass 1 records each rank's local tensors; pass 2 replays with true stacked results
    so the code under test performs its own nanmean/append on real gathered values.
    """
    ranks = [Rank(p) for p in pending_lists]
    n = len(ranks)

    # Pass 1: record what each rank would hand to each collective.
    for r in ranks:
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: (r.go_calls.append(obj), [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst])[1],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r, RecordingAccelerator(r, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)

    for r, pending in zip(ranks, pending_lists):
        assert r.go_calls == [sorted(pending)], (r.go_calls, sorted(pending))

    counts = [len(r.g_calls) for r in ranks]

    # Pass 2: replay with the true stacked tensors.
    for r in ranks:
        r2 = r.fresh()
        r._replay = r2
        ns = {
            "gather_object": lambda obj, r=r: [x for lst in pending_lists for x in lst],
            "torch": torch,
            "self": SimpleTrainer(r2, ReplayAccelerator(r2, ranks, n)),
            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),
        }
        exec(block, ns)
    return {i: dict(r._replay.metrics) for i, r in enumerate(ranks)}, counts

    def __init__(self, rank, accelerator):

        self._metrics = {"train": rank.metrics, "eval": _Metrics()}

        assert vals is not None, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} missing from {metrics}"
        assert len(vals) == 1, f"rank {rank}: metric {name!r} appended {len(vals)} times"

    assert res == {0: {}, 1: {}}, res

    print(f"case 4 OK  (nobody logs):      {res}  gather counts {counts}")

    """dict-of-lists behaving like defaultdict(list)."""

    def __missing__(self, key):
        self[key] = []
        return self[key]


class Rank:
    def __init__(self, pending):
        self.pending = dict(pending)
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.go_calls = []    # args passed to gather_object, in call order
        self.g_calls = []     # local tensors passed to accelerator.gather, in call order
        self.g_results = []   # tensors returned by accelerator.gather, in call order

    def fresh(self):
        """Reset state accumulated during the recording pass."""
        self.metrics = _Metrics()
        self.g_results = []
        return self


class RecordingAccelerator:
    """Pass-1 accelerator: records the local tensor, returns a placeholder of the shape
    the real gather would return (world_size,). Values appended this pass are discarded."""

    def __init__(self, rank, world_size):
        self._rank, self._world_size = rank, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):
        return torch.zeros(self._world_size, dtype=tensor.dtype)


class ReplayAccelerator:
    """Pass-2 accelerator: returns the true all-gathered stack for this call index."""

    def __init__(self, rank, recorded, world_size):
        self._rank, self._recorded, self._world_size = rank, recorded, world_size

    def gather(self, tensor):

        assert stack.shape == (self._world_size,), stack.shape

            "torch": torch,

            "mode": mode,
            "device": torch.device("cpu"),

            unwrapped_model = self.accelerator.unwrap_model(model)
            return self._forward_redirection(model, unwrapped_model, self.compute_liger_loss, unwrapped_model, inputs)
        return self._compute_loss(model, inputs)

    @staticmethod
    def get_off_policy_mask(
        advantages: torch.Tensor,
        per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
        sampling_per_token_logps: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.Tensor,
        off_policy_threshold: float,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Computes the Off-Policy Sequence Mask from DeepSeek-V3.2 paper. Returns a (B, 1) tensor where 1.0 indicates
        "Keep" and 0.0 indicates "Drop".
        """
        # forward KL div: log(pi_old) - log(pi_theta)
        kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps.detach()
        # Tokens vLLM could not score carry NaN and provide no KL evidence. Left in, the sequence mean is NaN,
        # `avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold` is then False, and a negative-advantage sequence would be dropped
        # on the strength of a single unscorable token.
        kl_div = torch.nan_to_num(kl_div, nan=0.0)
        # Sequence-level Mean KL (ignoring prompt+padding)
        seq_kl_sum = (kl_div * mask).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        avg_seq_kl = seq_kl_sum / mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1.0)
        # Keep if (Advantage >= 0) OR (KL <= delta)
        is_pos_adv = advantages >= 0
        is_low_kl = avg_seq_kl <= off_policy_threshold
        return (is_pos_adv | is_low_kl).to(dtype=mask.dtype)  # (B, 1)
